newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends broadly higher on weather.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends broadly higher on weather.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled broadly higher amid concerns over persistent dry weather in North Dakota and a lack of hedge-related selling, traders said.
Traders said only 15 percent of North Dakota received any precipitation over the weekend. That was far short of the widespread coverage that was expected last week.

"The dryness in western North Dakota and Montana is a worry, and we also saw (spillover) from delays to the Texas harvest...and reports of unevenness" coming from the soft red winter wheat tour in Ohio, an MGE trader said.
Traders in Kansas City said weather reports released at midday forecast continued dry conditions over the short term in North Dakota.
Spring wheat also held firm on a dearth of hedge-related pressure as growers waited for higher prices before selling.
MGE spring wheat settled 9-1/2 to 13-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with new crop September up 9-1/2 cents at $4.00-3/4.
Traders said LFG was a featured player, selling 1.6 million September bushels and buying 800,000 July.
